raw_case_text: A 40-year-old male patient was admitted to the orthopedic ward with chief complaints of pain, restriction of movements, and difficulty to bear weight on the left hip. The patient was a known case of SLE and on treatment with prednisolone 40 mg twice daily over the previous 6 years. In addition, he also had complaints of rashes over the trunk and pain in small joints of both hands for 2 months. The patient did not report any episode of fever over the preceding months. There was no history of trauma, prior surgery, or abdominal discomfort. There was no history of illness suggestive of typhoid fever in any of his family members. Local examination of the left hip region showed tenderness and the movements were painfully restricted. The laboratory findings were haemoglobin 9.8 gm%, white blood cell count 13,180 cells/cu.mm with neutrophilic leukocytosis. Peripheral smear showed microcytic normochromic anemia. Pus aspirated from the hip joint was inoculated in brain heart infusion broth, nutrient agar, 5% sheep blood agar, and MacConkey agar and incubated for 24 hours at 37 C. The gram stained smear of the pus showed plenty of polymorphonuclear leucocytes and gram negative bacilli. The culture yielded nonlactose fermenting colonies which was confirmed as Salmonella typhi by biochemical methods and serological typing. It was susceptible to ampicillin, trimethoprim-sulphamethoxazole, chloramphenicol, ciprofloxacin, cefotaxime, and ceftriaxone and resistant to nalidixic acid by disc diffusion method. The blood culture was found to be sterile. The Widal test was non-contributory. Fecal culture done on 3 consecutive days to detect carrier state or subclinical infection was negative. The radiograph and the magnetic resonance imaging of the left hip showed evidence of avascular necrosis of the neck of femur (Figure 1). In view of resistance to nalidixic acid, therapy with ciprofloxacin was not considered. Treatment with injection ceftriaxone 1 gram, intravenously twice daily was instituted and continued for 14 days. Surgical intervention was done (core decompression with free fibular grafting). The patient was explained about the guarded prognosis of the procedure. Histopathological examination of the biopsy specimen from the left neck and head of femur showed necrotic bone consistent with avascular necrosis. In view of the steroid induced avascular necrosis, patient was advised total hip replacement. However, the patient opted for discharge after relief from the pain.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 40-year-old man with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) presented with left hip pain, restricted range of motion, and inability to bear weight on the left leg, along with a 2-month history of truncal rash and bilateral small-joint hand pain.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient was admitted to the orthopedic ward with left hip pain, painfully restricted hip movements, and difficulty bearing weight on the left lower limb. He also reported rashes over his trunk and pain in the small joints of both hands for the preceding 2 months, without any episodes of fever.
subjective.past_medical_history: Known history of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) treated with oral prednisolone 40 mg twice daily for the past 6 years. No history of trauma, prior surgery, or family history of typhoid fever.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for left hip pain, inability to bear weight, truncal rash, and bilateral hand arthralgia. Pertinent negatives: no fever over the preceding months, no abdominal discomfort. Home medication: prednisolone 40 mg twice daily.

objective.physical_examination: Local examination of the left hip demonstrated joint tenderness and painfully restricted range of motion across planes.
objective.routine_investigations: Hemoglobin 9.8 g%, white blood cell count 13,180 cells/cu.mm with neutrophilic leukocytosis, and peripheral blood smear showing microcytic normochromic anemia. Blood culture was sterile, Widal test was non-contributory, and 3 consecutive daily stool cultures were negative. Plain radiograph of the left hip showed avascular necrosis of the femoral neck.
objective.advanced_workup: MRI of the left hip confirmed avascular necrosis of the left femoral neck. Hip joint aspiration yielded pus showing abundant polymorphonuclear leukocytes and Gram-negative bacilli on Gram stain; culture on blood/MacConkey/nutrient agar and brain-heart infusion broth grew non-lactose-fermenting colonies confirmed biochemically and serologically as Salmonella typhi, susceptible by disc diffusion to ampicillin, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, chloramphenicol, ciprofloxacin, cefotaxime, and ceftriaxone, and resistant to nalidixic acid. Histopathology of the left femoral head and neck biopsy specimen confirmed necrotic bone consistent with avascular necrosis.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Left hip septic arthritis and osteomyelitis due to nalidixic acid-resistant Salmonella typhi superimposed on corticosteroid-induced avascular necrosis (AVN) of the femoral head and neck in a patient with SLE, confirmed by hip aspirate pus culture/serotyping and bone biopsy histopathology. Because of nalidixic acid resistance, fluoroquinolones were avoided; the patient was treated with intravenous ceftriaxone 1 g twice daily for 14 days combined with surgical core decompression and free fibular grafting. Although total hip arthroplasty was recommended for the underlying steroid-induced AVN, the patient opted for discharge following resolution of his acute hip pain.
